title: The Delicate cup on the shelf
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：delicate　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 delicate 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the painter wrote of ① a delicate cup on the shelf in the catalogue, and everybody in the studio said at once that it was ② more delicate than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the painter, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the delicate ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most delicate cup on the shelf anybody in the studio had ever seen, or so the catalogue for May 1979 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too delicate to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the delicate ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a delicate matter of honour, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as delicate as the matter of honour they had once had in the old studio. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was delicate or not, and he said so.

By 1992 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue. What the line asked for was ⑦ something delicate, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next studio called the whole plan ⑧ quite delicate; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the catalogue kept the names of the delicate ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1995, in silence, she wrote of another delicate cup on the shelf in the same catalogue, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ more delicate than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most delicate matter of honour in the whole studio, she said in 1997, was the one she could never quite name; the delicate ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 精致（前置定语 a delicate cup on the shelf：1985 年画师在展品目录里记下的那件精致的杯子）
B. adj. 精致／微妙（比较级 more delicate than：文中两处，一处比架上的杯子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 精致／微妙（最高级 the most delicate：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 精致（表语 too delicate to do：母亲觉得它太精致，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 微妙（前置定语 a delicate matter of honour：叔叔把整件事称作一桩微妙的事）
F. adj. 微妙（同级比较 as delicate as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩名誉上的事相比）
G. adj. 微妙（后置定语 something delicate：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 微妙（受程度副词修饰 quite delicate：那位观者的评价）

answers.why: delicate 意为“精致”，1985 年画师在展品目录里记下的是“一件精致的杯子”，此处作前置定语 a delicate cup on the shelf。
delicate 意为“精致”，此处用比较级 more delicate than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
delicate 意为“精致”，展品目录上 五月 那行字说它是画室里最精致的一件，故用最高级 the most delicate cup on the shelf。
delicate 意为“精致”，母亲认为这件东西“太精致了，谁也用不上”，too delicate to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
delicate 意为“微妙”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩微妙的事”，此处作前置定语 a delicate matter of honour。
delicate 意为“微妙”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩名誉上的事一样微妙”，同级比较用 as delicate as。
delicate 意为“微妙”，展品目录上那半行字要的是“微妙的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something delicate。
delicate 意为“微妙”，邻画室来的那位观者认为这套计划“相当微妙”，quite 修饰原级 delicate。
delicate 意为“微妙”，1995 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要微妙”，故用比较级 more delicate than。
delicate 意为“微妙”，母亲 1997 年说的是“整个画室里最微妙的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most delicate matter of honour。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1985 年，画师在展品目录里记下了一件精致的杯子。（a delicate cup on the shelf）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更精致。（more delicate than …）
母亲觉得它太精致，谁也用不上。（too delicate to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩微妙的事。（a delicate matter of honour）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩名誉上的事一样微妙。（as delicate as …）
到了 1992 年，展品目录上只剩半行字：要的是一件微妙的东西。（something delicate）
answers: In 1985 the painter wrote of a delicate cup on the shelf in the catalogue.
Everybody said it was more delicate than the one named there the year before.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 delicate 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1985 the painter wrote of a delicate cup on the shelf in the catalogue, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most delicate cup on the shelf in the studio, or so the catalogue says.
My mother thought it too delicate to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a delicate matter of honour, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next studio called the plan quite delicate, and everybody laughed.
